chunks.text: Today we will talk about Nigeria.
Nigeria is a large and lively country in West Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Nigeria?
Nigeria is in West Africa.
It is next to Niger, Chad, Cameroon and Benin.
To the south, Nigeria touches the Atlantic Ocean.
Nigeria has cities, villages, forests, rivers and savannas.
What is the capital city of Nigeria?
The capital city is Abuja.
Abuja is in the center of the country.
It has government buildings, parks and wide roads.
But the biggest city in Nigeria is Lagos.
Lagos is very busy and full of life.
Other big cities include Kano, Ibadon and Port Harcourt.
How many people live in Nigeria?
Over 220 million people live in Nigeria.
It is the most populated country in Africa.
Many people live in cities, but many also live in villages.
Nigeria has many ethnic groups and cultures.
It is a diverse and vibrant country.
What language do people speak in Nigeria?
The official language is English.
English is used in schools, business and government.
But Nigeria also has over 500 local languages.
Some common ones are Hausa in the north, Yoruba in the southwest, Igbo in the southeast, Pigeon English, a simple mix of English and local words.
Many people speak more than one language every day.
What is the weather like in Nigeria?
Nigeria has a tropical climate.
It is usually hot all year.
There are two main seasons, rainy season, from April to October, dry season from November to March.
In the north, it is hot and dry.
In the south, it is hot and humid.
What does Nigeria look like?
Nigeria has many kinds of land.
Rain forests in the south, savannas, grasslands in the middle, deserts in the north, mountains and rivers like the Niger River and Benue River.
There are also farms, cities and coastal areas with beaches.
What animals live in Nigeria?
Nigeria has many animals such as monkeys, elephants, antelopes, crocodiles, hippos, birds, lizards and insects.
There are also domestic animals like goats, chickens and cows.
Many people raise animals in rural areas.
What do people eat in Nigeria?
Nigerian food is spicy, colorful and full of flavor.
Common foods include rice, yam, cassava and plantains, beans, vegetables and pepper sauce, fish, chicken and goat meat.
Popular dishes, jalaf rice, rice cooked with tomato, pepper and spices.
A goosey soup, soup made with melon seeds and vegetables.
Fufu, soft dough made from cassava or yam, eaten with soup.
Moimoi, steamed bean pudding, suya spicy grilled meat on sticks.
For drinks, people enjoy Zobo, hibiscus juice, kunu or fruit juice.
What is life like in Nigeria?
Life in Nigeria can be very busy in cities and more traditional in villages.
People go to school or work during the day.
In the evening they spend time with family and friends.
Nigerians enjoy music and dancing, storytelling, cooking and eating together, watching football, soccer.
Family is very important.
People help each other and stay close.
What are some holidays and traditions in Nigeria?
Independence Day, October 1st.
Eid al -Fitr and Eid al -Adha, celebrated by Muslims Christmas and Easter, celebrated by Christians.
New Yam Festival, celebrated in the Southeast.
People wear traditional clothes, sing, dance and eat special foods.
Popular clothing includes Agbada, Bubba, wrapper and head wraps.
Some fun facts about Nigeria.
Nigeria is called the Giant of Africa.
It has the largest economy in Africa.
Nollywood, Nigerian film industry is one of the biggest in the world.
Nigeria is home to many writers like Chinua Cebe and Chimamandan Gozi Adichi.
The Nigerian flag is green, white, green.
Now you know many things about Nigeria.
You know where it is, what people eat and what languages they speak.
You learned about the weather, animals, traditions and daily life.
Great job.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English podcast.
I am Emily.
